# Coding Standards

## General
- Functions should do ONE thing and do it well
- Maximum function length: 30 lines (excluding tests)
- Maximum file length: 300 lines (split if larger)
- Prefer composition over inheritance
- Use meaningful names: variables describe what, functions describe action
- No magic numbers — use named constants
- A TODO stays only when it links an issue (`TODO(#123): ...`)
- Error handling at system boundaries, trust internal code

## Python
- Use type hints for all function signatures
- Use `async def` for I/O-bound operations
- Use `uv` as the Python lifecycle tool (never raw pip, python -m venv, or virtualenv):
  - `uv init --app` — new project (creates pyproject.toml, .python-version)
  - `uv add <package>` — add dependencies (updates pyproject.toml + uv.lock, auto-creates .venv)
  - `uv sync` — install all deps from lockfile (auto-creates .venv if needed)
  - `uv run <command>` — execute within the venv (pytest, ruff, uvicorn, alembic, etc.)
  - Inside Dockerfiles: `uv sync --locked --no-dev --no-editable` (production) or `uv sync --locked` (dev)
- Follow PEP 8 naming: snake_case for functions/variables, PascalCase for classes
- Use Pydantic for validation at API boundaries
- Use `pathlib.Path` over `os.path`

## Rust
- `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` must pass
- Fallible paths return `Result`. `Regex::new` inside a `Lazy` static may panic: a bad pattern is a programmer error
- Guard behaviour lives in `src/` and is exported through PyO3. Do not reimplement it in Python

## TypeScript
- Use strict mode (`"strict": true` in tsconfig)
- Prefer `interface` over `type` for object shapes
- Use `const` by default, `let` only when mutation is needed
- Avoid `any` — use `unknown` and narrow with type guards
- Use barrel exports sparingly (causes tree-shaking issues)

## Testing
- Test behavior, not implementation
- One assertion per test (conceptually)
- Use descriptive test names: "should [expected behavior] when [condition]"
- AAA pattern: Arrange, Act, Assert
- No logic in tests (no if/else, no loops)
